items.text:
Ostranauts has a steep learning curve, unique delivery of story/character content, and a number of bugs that need to be hashed out. Aside from the tutorial (which has improved significantly since the beginning), it does not hold your hand. It gave me difficulty in my first 5-10 hours, and I lost steam with it for a while. That being said, when I pushed through that and got a handle on the UI, character management, fully explored ship building, and started some questlines it became apparent there's a lot more going on with this game than some people give it credit for.

This game is a slow burn. Usually it respects your time, sometimes it doesn't (went to Titan shipyard to buy a corvette and only junkers were for sale) - you are insignificant and the sandbox world around will just spiral sometimes (random dead stations for example - though I haven't come across this). But when you survive that first trip to another planet, your first micrometorite strike, or get chased down by pirates only to fight them off with a katana and win/take their ship - it nets you that feeling few games seem to nail these days.

It's enjoyable to fix up a floating wreck and make it your own, build out your starter coffin, find that one piece of salvage you were looking for, or take out a giant loan on something luxury. Same for those frantic moments where you have to decide whether or not to vent your cabin because you let a piece of conduit go too long so there's a fire, but you also have a limited amount of nitrogen/oxygen to replenish your atmosphere. It captures the spectrum of hard sci-fi experiences we imagine pretty well; from the monotony of inter-planetary travel and those time of pure panic and uncertainty if you and your crew is going to make it to your destination. In some ways, it's like a version of The Sims where your home is your ship and you could die over a seemingly insignificant oversight -- or a system authority vessel could collide with you at 1 km/s.

If you like the following games or some of their mechanics you may like this one: Project Zomboid, Kenshi, KSP, Hardspace Shipbreaker. If you like The Expanse or other grounded sci-fi you may like this as well. Results not guaranteed, but I like this title. 

If you'd like to see someone who is earnest in their assessment of the game and quirks but clearly still enjoys it, check out Rhadamat's YouTube channel to see how it may fit for you.
items.text_zh:
《Ostranauts》学习曲线陡峭，故事/角色内容的呈现方式独特，还有不少需要解决的bug。除了教程（自最初以来已显著改进）之外，它不会手把手教你。在我最初的5到10个小时里，它让我感到困难，我一度对它失去了热情。话虽如此，当我挺过那段时期，掌握了UI、角色管理，全面探索了飞船建造，并开始了一些任务线之后，就明显能看出这款游戏的内容比一些人认为的要多得多。

这款游戏是慢热型的。通常它会尊重你的时间，有时则不会（去泰坦造船厂想买一艘护卫舰，结果只有破烂货在卖）——你无足轻重，周围的沙盒世界有时就是会失控（比如随机出现的死寂空间站——虽然我还没遇到过）。但当你挺过第一次前往另一个星球的旅程、第一次微陨石撞击，或者被海盗追上来，却只用一把武士刀击退他们并获胜/夺走他们的飞船时——它会带给你如今很少有游戏似乎能抓住的那种感觉。

修好一艘漂浮的残骸并把它变成你自己的、扩建你的初始棺材舱、找到你一直在找的那一件 salvage，或者为某件奢侈品背上一大笔贷款，这些都很有乐趣。那些疯狂的时刻也是如此：你必须决定是否要给船舱泄压，因为你让一段管道拖得太久所以起火了，但你的氮气/氧气储量也有限，需要补充大气。它相当好地捕捉到了我们想象中的硬科幻体验的整个光谱；从行星际旅行的单调乏味，到那种纯粹恐慌和不确定你和你的船员能否抵达目的地的时刻。在某些方面，它就像是一个版本的《模拟人生》，只不过你的家就是你的飞船，你可能会因为一个看似微不足道的疏忽而死掉——或者一艘系统当局的飞船可能以1公里/秒的速度撞上你。

如果你喜欢以下游戏或它们的某些机制，你可能会喜欢这款：Project Zomboid、Kenshi、KSP、Hardspace Shipbreaker。如果你喜欢《苍穹浩瀚》或其他接地气的科幻作品，你也可能会喜欢这款。结果不保证，但我喜欢这款作品。

如果你想看看一个对这款游戏及其怪癖做出真诚评价、但显然仍然很享受它的人，可以去看看Rhadamat的YouTube频道，看看它是否适合你。
